owner: Edit mastery (decision 17). Taste here is Ishaan's: every device, number and sound below comes from a film he approved (v8 podcast tiles, v9 Hinglish podcast 8/10, v10 em5 interview 9/10, lab vlog v1 'Good').
who: The free server model picks from this menu; the code fills only the slots. A capable model (Claude on the bridge, or a user's own strong model) does NOT use this menu: it writes the full spec from the ishaan-motion skill (edit-fundamentals §3, §10-§12) and invents each graphic for the video. Owner, 2026-10-18: 'for a free model we will make it more library focus ... using the capable model's generation, not building from scratch, just directing it; for capable Claude it will push more on creativity.'
rules: Every pick answers 'what does this sentence need?' on this clip; two clips never get the same film (no fixed order, no device on every film).
At most one device per sentence; a plain speaker or punch beat between two devices; never the same device twice in a row.
The first beat is the speaker (start on the speaker's first kept line); the last beat is the speaker.
One text layer per frame (the player hides the caption under text graphics); text never covers a face (the player moves it).
Captions in the spoken language as spoken: Hinglish in Latin letters, never translated.
Colours come from the brand's site and logo, else the footage (the code reads them; the model never names a colour).
On-screen words come from the speaker's own words in that sentence ({hero}, {phrase}, {name}); the model never writes new copy.

slots.{line}: anchor of the sentence's first word: { "w": word, "after": seconds } so repeats resolve
slots.{hero}: anchor of the sentence's stressed word (the one the sentence is about)
slots.{hero2}: anchor of a second key word later in the same sentence
slots.{last}: anchor of the sentence's last word
slots.{name}: a person or place named in the sentence, as spoken (text)
slots.{role}: what the speaker says that name is (text, optional, else omit the field)
slots.{phrase}: two to three of the speaker's own words from the sentence (text)
slots.{number}: a number said in the sentence (text)
slots.{unit}: the word after the number, as spoken (text)
slots.{still}: a clip time in seconds whose frame shows what the sentence is about
slots.{chars}: the letters or initials the sentence spells (text)
slots.{items}: two or three of the speaker's own short items from a list in the sentence (text array)
slots.{sfx:<event>}: a sound for that event from the library (assetsForEvent, per video, not the last one used); the code puts the file in spec.sounds under that event key and writes the key here. Events: whoosh, hit, pop, drop, click, chime, typing, paper, riser, snap
slots.{music:<mood>}: a bed from the library matched to the clip's mood (spec.music.file); gain 0.06-0.08, start 2
slots.{footage:<query>}: a real clip from the footage finder (src/footage) for what the sentence names, else a span of the clip itself that shows it; never a drawn stand-in

captions.pending: 2, 3 and 4 join this list when the player draws them through spec.caption.preset (Edit mastery is adding it; 3 and 4 need the person matte)

not_yet: Library camera moves and UI rows have no device in the player yet, so the menu does not offer {camera:} or {ui:} slots; they are added here when the player can draw them.

devices.use: a sentence that carries itself; the default between devices
one stressed word that lands the sentence (a claim, a surprise, a verdict)
a person or a place is named and is on screen
the sentence does maths or one number becomes another (half of, from X to Y)
the sentence is about a filter, a look or choosing one option of several
the sentence describes the picture changing (dreamy, filtered, dramatic) and the change can be shown
before against after, raw against a named version, this against that
the sentence spells letters, initials or a short code
a list of two or three short items said one after another
the speaker states one or two short states or feelings about themselves (ready, excited, done)
the sentence names a thing, place or activity real footage can show (at most three per film, each its own beat)

desk_item.doodle: one or two short marker strokes that underline, point or tick (paths in the place's doodle box)
desk_item.label: {phrase}

devices.after: the next beat is the speaker with a leak

devices.use: only as the return to the speaker after a desk-print or a full-screen device; at most three per film
